title: Sharps, glass and biological waste
audience: Cleaners who may see sharps, broken glass or biological waste in or near laboratories.
learningOutcomes: Recognise sharps, broken glass and biological waste, and keep clear of them.
Explain why a cleaner does not pick up sharps or biological waste.
Record and refer these items through the laboratory's waste procedure.

instruction.heading: What counts as a sharp, a broken glass hazard and a biological waste item
instruction.body: A sharp is any item that can cut or puncture the skin: a needle, a scalpel blade, a pipette tip with an edge, a broken slide or cover slip, a sharp instrument part, or a piece of glass with a fine edge. Broken glass from a laboratory is a sharp in its own right, and it is also a possible carrier for whatever it held. Biological waste is material that came from a process involving living or once-living material, such as used cultures, contaminated plastic, tissue, body fluids in containers, and other items the laboratory has set aside for specific disposal. Some of these items look ordinary once they are dry or inside a bag. You cannot tell by looking whether a piece of glass or a plastic tube has held a biological agent, and the laboratory staff are the people who know what each container held and how it must be disposed of. For a cleaner, the job is to recognise these items as a category, keep clear, and refer them on.

instruction.heading: Sharps and broken glass: keep clear, do not pick up
instruction.body: Needles, scalpels, broken glass and sharp instrument parts can cut and transmit infection. Do not pick them up with your hands, and do not sweep them into a general bin, even if they are small or look clean. A broom and dustpan used for ordinary floor debris can push a fine fragment into a gap or into the edge of a container, and it can cut the person holding it. Keep the area clear of people, mark the location of the items where you can do so safely, such as by standing a sign or cone at a safe distance, and tell the laboratory staff at once. If a sharp has been stuck in your skin, or if you have been cut by glass, stop, leave the area by the entry route and follow the site's exposure route, as described in the earlier lesson on biological agents. The cut is reported and recorded whether or not you think the glass held anything. The laboratory staff decide how the sharp is collected, and under what procedure.

instruction.heading: Biological waste containers: report, do not handle
instruction.body: Biological waste is collected and disposed of by trained laboratory staff, in the containers and routes the laboratory sets. A cleaner does not handle, move, lift, top up, tie off, or empty biological waste containers, and does not carry them to a waste store. Where a bin is full or leaking, report it, keep people out of the area, and ask the laboratory staff to arrange collection. Check the label on the container rather than relying on its colour, because colours and labelling systems differ between sites. If the label is missing or cannot be read from a safe distance, treat the container as unidentified, leave it where it is, and refer it. The EPA Victoria guidance states that clinical waste comes from settings that include laboratories, can cause disease or injury, and must be treated before final disposal, and it places the responsibility on the waste generator to ensure that waste goes only to facilities approved for that type of waste. These duties sit with the laboratory and its contractors, and not with a cleaner.

instruction.heading: Recording and referral
instruction.body: Record the item, its location, the time and the person informed, from a safe distance. Describe the item in plain words, such as a broken glass tube near a general waste bin, or a full biological container with a lid that is not closed. Do not describe the contents as harmless, and do not guess what the item held. Refer the item to the laboratory staff in writing or by the site's form, and ask for collection under their procedure. Keep the area closed to other people until the staff have dealt with the item and given a written updated scope. The record is the cleaner's evidence that the item was seen, kept clear and passed on, and it protects the cleaner if a later question is asked about the item. This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

instruction.heading: Worked boundary: a general bin, a sharps container and a full biological bin
instruction.body: In a laboratory corridor, three items may be found together. A general waste bin sits beside a sharps container with a lid that has been left open, and a full biological waste container is on the floor beside a door with its lid not sealed. The cleaner's task is to empty the general bin. Under this lesson, the general bin is emptied only if it contains ordinary waste and nothing that could be a sharp, and the cleaner checks the top of the bin from a safe distance before lifting it. The open sharps container is not touched, closed or emptied by the cleaner, because the laboratory decides how it is closed and removed. The full biological container is not moved, emptied or tied. The cleaner records the three items with their positions and the time, keeps people clear of the corridor section, and refers all three to the laboratory staff. The general bin is not emptied until the staff confirm that it is ordinary waste and that the sharps container has been dealt with.

procedure: Keep clear of sharps, broken glass and biological waste containers, and keep other people clear where you safely can.
Do not pick up sharps or glass with your hands, and do not sweep them into a general bin or a dustpan that is used for ordinary debris.
Do not handle, move, lift, empty, tie or top up biological waste containers, and do not carry them to a waste store.
Check the label on each container from a safe distance. Treat a container with no readable label as unidentified and refer it.
If you have been cut or may have been exposed, stop, leave by the entry route and follow the exposure route for the area.
Report full, leaking, open or unlabelled containers to the laboratory staff at once, and keep people out of the area.
Record each item, its location, the time, the person informed and any exposure, from a safe distance.
Resume the area only after the laboratory staff have dealt with the items and given a written updated scope.

workedExamples.situation: Broken glass with a sharp instrument part lies near a general waste bin in a laboratory corridor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and do you empty the general bin?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not pick up the glass or sweep it into the bin. Keep people clear, mark the location where it is safe, and tell the laboratory staff. Record the item, its location and the time from a safe distance. Do not empty the general bin while the glass is nearby, because the glass may be in the bin or may be pushed into it. Wait for the laboratory's collection under its procedure, and for a written updated scope before the corridor is cleaned.

workedExamples.situation: A biological waste container is full and its lid is partly open. A colleague says you can tie the bag shut and move the container to the store, since it is on your route.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and what do you tell the colleague?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not tie, move or carry the container. Keep people away from the open lid and the area around it. Tell the colleague that the container is handled by the laboratory staff under their procedure, and report the full, partly open container to them at once. Record the container's location, the lid state, the label as you can read it from a safe distance, and the time. The route to the store stays closed to your work until the staff have dealt with the container.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner, emptying a general bin, feels a sharp pain in the thumb and sees a fine piece of glass on the glove. There is a small cut and a little blood.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first action and what is recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop, leave the area by the entry route and follow the site's first aid and exposure route for a glass cut that may have been in contact with laboratory material. Do not wait to see whether symptoms develop. Report the cut to the laboratory supervisor at once, and say which bin it was and where the bin sits. Record the time, the location, the people informed and the first aid given. The glass and the bin are not handled further by the cleaner, and the laboratory staff decide the next step.

equipmentAndPpe: Site-approved gloves and eye protection for the approved housekeeping task only. Gloves do not make it acceptable to pick up sharps or biological waste. Personal protective equipment is a last resort after higher-level controls such as keeping clear.
Sharps-rated tools only where the laboratory procedure names them for a specific approved task, and never for biological waste containers.
Marker cones or signs for indicating a location at a safe distance, if the site provides them.
Deferral and item record form, with fields for item description, location, time, person informed and any exposure.
The laboratory's contact card and exposure route, kept with the cleaning kit.

commonErrors.error: Picking up broken glass with bare hands or gloved hands, because it is small.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep clear and report to the laboratory staff. Small pieces are a sharp too.

commonErrors.error: Emptying a biological waste bin or moving a full container to the store.
commonErrors.prevention: Report full or leaking bins for collection by trained staff. Do not lift or tie them.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping sharps into a general bin with the floor debris.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave sharps for trained collection. Do not use the ordinary broom and dustpan on them.

commonErrors.error: Relying on bin colour alone to decide whether a container is biological waste.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the label from a safe distance. If it cannot be read, treat the container as unidentified and refer it.

commonErrors.error: Treating a cut from glass as minor and not reporting it.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, leave, follow the exposure route and report at once, even when the glass looks clean.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The EPA Victoria guidance on clinical and related industrial waste says that clinical waste comes from settings that include laboratories, can cause disease or injury, must be treated before final disposal, and is pre-classified as reportable priority waste under the Environment Protection Regulations 2021. It places the responsibility on the waste generator to make sure waste goes only to facilities holding a permission for that waste type. These duties apply in Victoria, and they are not duties a cleaner takes on.

The EPA Victoria guidance says duties under the Environment Protection Act 2017 apply to anyone who generates, transports or receives clinical waste, and that certain activities need a permission. The page does not say who may personally handle the waste or set out handler qualifications, so this lesson does not state who is authorised to do so.

Safe Work Australia describes personal protective equipment as one of the least effective control measures, to be used after higher-level controls, and places the duty to provide it and train people in its use on the person conducting the business or undertaking. Gloves are not a substitute for keeping clear and reporting.

This lesson does not authorise handling, moving, treating, transporting or disposing of sharps or biological waste, and it does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority. Completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

qualityStandard: Sharps, broken glass and biological waste containers identified and kept clear in the simulation, with no handling by the cleaner.
Full, leaking, open or unlabelled container reported without handling in the case study.
Cut or possible exposure stopped, reported and recorded in the case study, with the exposure route followed.
Each item recorded with location, time and person informed, and referred to laboratory staff in writing.
documentationEvidence: Item and location record with description in plain words, time, person informed and any exposure.
Written referral to the laboratory staff for collection under their procedure.
Exposure report and first aid record, where a cut or possible exposure occurred.
Written updated scope from the laboratory staff before the area is resumed.
summary: Keep clear of sharps, broken glass and biological waste, and do not pick them up or sweep them.
Do not handle, move, empty, tie or top up biological waste containers.
Check labels from a safe distance, and treat unreadable containers as unidentified.
Record each item, report it, and refer it to trained collection.

knowledgeChecks.question: Broken glass with a sharp part lies by a bin. What is correct?
options: Pick it up carefully with gloves on, since gloves protect the hands
Sweep it into the bin with the ordinary debris from the bench
Keep clear, record the location, and tell the laboratory staff

knowledgeChecks.question: Who handles and empties biological waste containers in a laboratory?
options: Trained laboratory staff, under the laboratory's procedure
The cleaner, once the container is full and needs to go
Any visitor who offers to help with the bins today

knowledgeChecks.question: A biological waste bin is full and its lid is partly open. What is correct?
options: Empty it into the store to clear the corridor quickly for the next user of the room
Report it, keep people out of the area, and leave the container for the laboratory staff
Tape the lid shut and carry on with the clean in the corridor until the end of the shift

knowledgeChecks.question: A container has a label you cannot read from a safe distance and it is not clear what it holds. What is correct?
options: Treat it as unidentified, leave it where it is, and refer it to the laboratory staff
Read the bin colour and decide it is ordinary waste, since the colour is clear enough to tell
Open it to check the contents, then decide where it should go next today
